text: Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Hi — trying to generate a debug bundle from our private deployment collectors, upload to the presigned URL is failing with 403. Happened around 09:12 UTC. We need this for an escalated support case. Maya (Support): Thanks Priya — can you paste the collector run ID / request id from the logs and the exact error you see when the upload fails? Also which collector version are you running? Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): run id: run-20260315-09-12-53 Collector version: 1.6.3-rc2 Error when using wget to PUT the archive: ``` --2026-03-15 09:13:01-- https://presign.example-cust.com/abc123 Resolving presign.example-cust.com... 10.1.2.3 Connecting to presign.example-cust.com|10.1.2.3|:443... connected. HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 403 Forbidden 2026-03-15 09:13:02 ERROR 403: Forbidden. ``` We also tried curl -X PUT --upload-file debugbundle.tar.gz "" and got 403 with XML: AccessDenied Maya (Support): Got it. Two quick possibilities: presign expired or there is a policy restricting PUT by User-Agent. Can you paste the presign URL (or the presign id) and the timestamps in the collector log around the upload attempt? Also send the collector debug log with --log-level debug if possible (we only need the 20 lines around the upload attempt). Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Presign id: presign-abc123-exp-20260315T0912Z Log snippet attached below: ``` 2026-03-15T09:12:50Z collector starting bundle run-id=run-20260315-09-12-53 2026-03-15T09:12:57Z redact: starting redaction mode=partial 2026-03-15T09:13:00Z bundle: archive debugbundle.tar.gz size=124MB 2026-03-15T09:13:01Z uploader: presign request success id=presign-abc123 url=https://presign.example-cust.com/abc123 2026-03-15T09:13:01Z uploader: upload start method=wget url=.../abc123 2026-03-15T09:13:01Z uploader: upload failure http_status=403 body=AccessDenied 2026-03-15T09:13:02Z collector: retry upload attempt=1 ``` Jorge (Eng): Quick check — Priya, can you try the curl command with the following headers and share output? We want to see if signing or content-type mismatch is the issue: ``` curl -v -X PUT -T debugbundle.tar.gz "" -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" -H "User-Agent: collector/1.6.3-rc2" ``` Also can you run `openssl s_client -connect presign.example-cust.com:443 -showcerts` and paste the cert chain? Sometimes internal TLS interception rewrites requests and breaks signed presigns. Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Ran the curl above, got same 403. Verbose shows server responded immediately with 403, no intermediate redirects. Attached the openssl output — cert is our corporate TLS terminator with CN=corp-proxy.local Maya (Support): That aligns with a proxy or WAF blocking the PUT. Two paths: (A) we can have ops generate a fresh presign with a relaxed ACL for this debug run (short-lived, 10m) and a different key prefix so proxy rules don't trigger, or (B) we can use the collector's SFTP fallback to upload directly to your support SFTP endpoint. Which do you prefer? Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Ops says we can't change proxy rules quickly. SFTP fallback sounds faster. How do we enable it? collector-bot: To generate a debug bundle and force SFTP upload, run: ``` collector --run-id run-20260315-09-12-53 --bundle --upload-method sftp --sftp-host sftp.support.redwood.example --sftp-user support-upload --sftp-path /incoming/greendocs/ --redact full --log-level debug ``` Notes: - Use `--redact full` to avoid sending PII. - SFTP credentials should be shared via secure channel (do NOT paste in Slack). Jorge (Eng): If you enable SFTP, collector will create the bundle locally and run an scp/sftp transfer. Make sure the collector instance has outbound SSH allowed and the correct SSH key in /etc/collector/keys/support_upload_id_rsa (or pass --sftp-key ). Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Starting run now with SFTP. Will DM the SSH key to Maya. Nathan (Ops): FYI I pre-created the directory /incoming/greendocs and set a two-hour write-only ACL. Share the SFTP username and I'll watch for the upload. Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Upload attempt succeeded via SFTP at 09:19 UTC. Collector log: ``` 2026-03-15T09:18:55Z uploader: sftp connect host=sftp.support.redwood.example user=support-upload 2026-03-15T09:18:56Z uploader: sftp upload start local=debugbundle.tar.gz remote=/incoming/greendocs/debugbundle-run-20260315-09-12-53.tar.gz 2026-03-15T09:19:01Z uploader: sftp upload success bytes=129847623 duration_ms=5400 ``` Maya (Support): Received the bundle and started redaction verification. Quick note on the original presign failure: looks like the corporate TLS terminator rewrites or blocks PUTs with our collector User-Agent. Ops — can we add a transient rule to whitelist presign.example-cust.com for PUTs from that collector User-Agent pattern? If not, we should add guidance for customers behind corporate proxies to use SFTP fallback or use `User-Agent` override in the collector config. Jorge (Eng): I'll file a small docs patch: add a note in the private deployment troubleshooting doc about proxy/WAF causing presign 403s and include the curl repro snippet and the SFTP fallback command. Also we'll add a collector flag `--user-agent-override` so teams can workaround proxies without rebuilding. Priya (Acct: GreenDocs): Confirming the bundle has redacted PII and we gave Maya the secure link to the SFTP transfer log. Thanks everyone for the fast assist. :thumbsup: Maya (Support): Marking this thread resolved for now. If anything else pops up while we inspect the bundle contents, we'll reopen. Thanks Priya and team! :heart:
